articles.title: BBC Inside Science - Are we alone in the universe? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: What if the Goldilocks zone is for idiots?
articles.body: Scientists have long referred to the Goldilocks zone – the region around a star where conditions are not too hot and not too cold but “just right” for life. Joined by a live audience at the Cheltenham Science Festival in the UK, Tom Whipple asks what are the true limitations of alien life? How do we spot it? And have we been looking too narrowly? Planetary scientist at MIT Sara Seagar discusses her team’s mission to Venus where, on the surface, temperatures can reach 500 degrees Celsius and it rains sulphuric acid. Above the rain, up in the clouds, Sara Seagar tells us how there could be life. And Lewis Dartnell, Professor of astrobiology at the University of Westminster, describes how he looks for extremophiles. These are organisms on earth that are found in places we once thought impossibly hostile to life. Plus, the missions to find life on Mars.... Presenter: Tom Whipple Producer: Dan Welsh Editor: Ilan Goodman & Martin Smith Production Coordinator: Jana Bennett-Holesworth

articles.title: Alien: Romulus is a solid franchise tribute plagued by weird optics
articles.summary: Alien: Romulus — out August 16th — is a visual stunner teeming with disgusting jump scares, but its central drama falls flat.
articles.body: It’s mind-boggling that Alien: Romulus almost wound up debuting on Hulu instead of theaters. The film’s intricate set design alone makes it one of the series’ most visually impressive chapters, and its practical effects are a welcome change of pace in a summer blockbuster season that has been dominated by uninspired CGI spectacle. Director Fede Álvarez’s new standalone entry in the long-running sci-fi / horror franchise feels especially primed to speak to a new generation of fans. But as fun as Romulus is to look at, its story plays more like a compilation of the Alien series’ greatest hits than a movie that’s trying to sing its own tune. And the few new ideas Romulus does bring to the table are undercut by its insistence on leaning into some very questionable optics. Set sometime between the first two Alien entries, Romulus is another horrific tale of how a group of unsuspecting people’s lives are ruined (and, in some cases, ended) by the Weyland-Yutani Corporation’s fixation on profits and biological weapons. On Jackson’s Star, the Wey-Yu-owned mining colony, desperate workers like Rain Carradine (Cailee Spaeny) are forced to spend decades laboring to earn their freedom to leave. There are plenty of monsters — bureaucratic ones — prioritizing the company’s interests. It’s not uncommon for people to die down in the mines, and life up on the colony’s grimy, sunless surface isn’t much better. [Media: Even when it seems as if freedom is within reach, there’s never any guarantee that Weyland-Yutani will actually do right by its all-but-enslaved employees. Rain learns that the company’s newly calculated quotes will keep her on the colony years longer than she anticipated, and she knows deep down that her faceless corporate overlords have no real intentions of ever letting her or her synthetic adoptive brother Andy (David Jonsson) escape. Romulus’ focus on younger characters sets it apart from previous Alien installments, and though the story doesn’t directly connect to any of the older films, it’s inferred that people’s hopeless lives of toil and struggle on colonies like Jackson’s Star are part of what makes voyages like the Nostromo’s possible. Rain, Andy, and all of the film’s other space-born twentysomethings (Archie Renaux, Isabela Merced, Spike Fearn, Aileen Wu) know they’ll die before they see a penny of the money they generate for their corporate overlords. That bleak reality makes it all too easy for the youths to come up with a convoluted plan to fly up to a decommissioned space station named Renaissance in hopes of finding a way to zoom off to a better future. But things, of course, do not go as planned. From its striking opening scene up in orbit, Alien: Romulus’ space horror atmosphere is exquisite thanks in no small part to its massive, intricately designed practical sets. They give the film’s various locations a sense of actual place and a sense of lived-in-ness. Every shot of Jackson’s Star makes it feel like a smoggy, apocalyptic wasteland where the air itself might kill you. In contrast to the colony’s sludge and filth, there’s a retrofuturistic sheen to places within the Renaissance, the film’s abandoned space station. But beneath the thick layers of dust, slimy nightmares await Rain and her friends. And, as tends to be the case with Alien films, Romulus’ humans quickly realize why it’s never really a good idea to mess around with Wey-Yu property. Because so many of Romulus’ beats echo iconic moments from past Alien movies, very few of the new film’s twists and turns will take longtime fans by surprise as the Renaissance is transformed into a nest teeming with Xenomorphs. Unlike many of Aliens’ previous protagonists, Rain’s crew is so green that they’re essentially helpless to fend off swarms of facehuggers awakened by the kids’ fumbling around. It all makes for a structurally solid enough origin for a new Ripley-esque hero, but the substance of Romulus’ story — which is meant to keep you invested in these people’s lives — falls a bit flat. [Image: Both Spaeny and Jonsson bring compelling energies to their performances as Rain, a steely audience insert, and Andy, a peculiar synth whose outdated hardware leaves him prone to seizures and bouts of social awkwardness that read almost like a kind of neurodivergence. But as many times as Rain refers to Andy as her “brother,” Romulus does a piss poor job of ever presenting the characters’ relationship in a way that makes it feel like one built on believable, reciprocal love. Andy is programmed to follow Rain around and tell knock-knock jokes to lift her spirits; Rain is usually there to reboot him when he glitches out. But she is slow to defend the synth from her fellow humans who delight in poking, prodding, and zapping her brother as a way of raging at the unfairness of their lives. Their relationship is often unconvincing and sometimes completely off-putting. With Andy, Romulus attempts to riff on the way that past Alien films have framed synths like Ian Holm’s Ash and Michael Fassbender’s David as humanoid avatars of Weyland-Yutani’s nefariousness. Here, that idea is reflected in the way that everyone around Andy treats him like a simple-minded child, programmed solely to keep his sister happy. Executed differently, this dynamic might have worked to make Rain and Andy feel like a duo who keep each other safe. But the abuse Romulus heaps on its sole Black character in service of iffy worldbuilding and plot advancement is its most glaring weakness. Strangely, Romulus winds up spending so much time showing you how much humans hate synths like Andy that the movie’s left with almost no space to properly develop its other characters enough to make their battles with Xenomorphs particularly memorable. The practical aliens themselves are magnificent, and Álvarez finds several inventive ways to showcase how terrifying the creatures can still be even 50 years after they first appeared on-screen. As the movie rushes to a classic Alien final battle, though, Romulus becomes so comfortable whipping those old tricks out that it feels as if it’s trying to coast on nostalgia rather than flying under its own steam. That might turn off longtime fans hoping to see something new after years of watching ovomorphs bloom open and chestbursters claw their way out of people’s bodies. But for folks really just looking for a few solid jump scares and a big, artful celebration of the impact Ridley Scott’s imagination has had on the sci-fi / horror genre, Alien: Romulus is enough.

articles.title: Alien is coming back to Earth for a second season
articles.summary: Alien: Earth has been renewed for a second season, which will film in London next year, as returning showrunner Noah Hawley inks a new deal with Disney.
articles.body: More than a month after the first season’s finale aired, FX has finally confirmed that Alien: Earth will get a second run of episodes, ending some sleepless nights for this reporter / Alien obsessive. No release date has been set for the second season yet, though it will film some time next year. Showrunner Noah Hawley is returning to lead the series again, and the holdup on the announcement might have been because it brings with it confirmation that he’s signed a new ongoing deal with Disney. The Hollywood Reporter suggests the deal could see him move beyond FX, where he’s worked on Fargo, Legion, and now Alien, to work across Disney’s other networks and platforms. “FX has always supported bold, character-driven storytelling. From the very beginning with Fargo, they’ve encouraged me to take creative risks and follow the story wherever it leads,” said Hawley. “I’m grateful to continue exploring the world of Alien: Earth alongside our partners, cast, and crew as we begin the next chapter.” Production for the second season will move from Thailand to London, though we’ll have to wait and see if that was a purely practical choice, or one that suggests the show will be moving on from the Neverland island where its Prodigy corporation is headquartered. It’s not the only Alien in development right now, with a sequel also in the works to 2024 movie Romulus.

articles.title: Autêntico, Ney Matogrosso rejeita o marketing da despedida ao anunciar a turnê '85 anos de ousadia' para 2027 | G1
articles.body:
Ney Matogrosso estreia a turnê '85 anos de ousadia' em 30 de janeiro no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo (RJ) — Foto: David LaChapelle / Divulgação

♬ Ainda em cena com o show “Bloco na rua”, estreado em 2019, Ney Matogrosso emenda o espetáculo atual com turnê inédita, intitulada “85 anos de ousadia” e prevista para percorrer arenas e estádios do Brasil com dez apresentações ao longo de 2027. O nome da turnê alude ao fato de o cantor ter completado 85 anos de vida em 1º de agosto, em plena atividade, lotando shows pelo Brasil e com planos de gravar álbum com o repertório da cantora Angela Ro Ro (1949 – 2025), falecida no ano passado, aos 75 anos.

Contudo, o cantor já deixa evidente que inexistem planos de encerrar com o próximo show a carreira iniciada em 1973 com vocalista do grupo Secos & Molhados. “Não estou me despedindo”, avisa Ney, autêntico como sempre, rejeitando o marketing da última grande turnê pelo Brasil, recorrente na promoção de excursões de artistas já octogenários.

O que impressiona positivamente em Ney Matogrosso é a simplicidade. Todo um aparato midiático foi criado para anunciar a turnê à imprensa no início da noite de hoje, 26 de agosto, mas o cantor permaneceu sem afetação, sem pose de popstar e sem mania de grandeza durante a entrevista coletiva. Ao contrário. Ney ficou o todo tempo na dele, sem querer impressionar, deixando que os outros falassem mais por ele, e dele, do que ele próprio.

Pelo cronograma inicial, serão dez shows da turnê “85 anos de ousadia”, mas, por ora, foram anunciadas somente cinco datas. A estreia nacional da turnê “85 anos de ousadia” está agendada para 30 de janeiro, no estádio Nubank Parque, em São Paulo. Já a derradeira apresentação do show acontece no estádio Maracanã, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), em 18 de dezembro.

Entre a estreia e o último show, Ney subirá ao palco da Arena da Baixada, em Curitiba (RJ) em 3 de abril; da casa Classic Hall em Olinda (PE) em 17 de abril e na Esplanada do Mineirão, em Belo Horizonte (MG), em 1º de maio.

Promovida com imagens inéditas do fotógrafo norte-americano David LaChapelle, feitas em ensaio no Jardim Botânico de São Paulo, a turnê “85 anos de ousadia” mostrará Ney em cena com dez figurinos inéditos – um para cada apresentação do show – e alusivos a figurinos marcantes na trajetória do cantor nos palcos. O figurino do primeiro show remeterá ao do espetáculo “Bandido” (1976), segundo show solo de Ney, estreado há 50 anos.

Aos 85 anos, a maior ousadia de Ney Matogrosso é permanecer imune ao vírus do estrelismo e da egotrip que tem feito incontáveis vítimas no universo pop.

articles.title: Festival reúne cultura, história e música em Fernando de Noronha | G1
articles.standfirst: Segunda edição do evento acontece no domingo (30), na Praça São Miguel, com programação gratuita a partir das 15h.
articles.summary: Segunda edição do evento Festei acontece no domingo (30), na Praça São Miguel, com programação gratuita a partir das 15h.
articles.body:
Festival será realizado em Noronha no domingo (30) — Foto: Cristiano Régis/Acervo pessoal

A segunda edição do Festival Festei será realizada no domingo (30), na Praça São Miguel, em Fernando de Noronha . O evento começa às 15h e terá palestras, manifestações culturais, oficinas e apresentações musicais. A programação é gratuita.

Segundo os organizadores, o festival tem como objetivo resgatar a memória da comunidade noronhense, valorizando histórias, personagens, tradições e saberes da ilha.

“A programação foi construída a partir da valorização da identidade local. O festival propõe um encontro entre gerações e diferentes formas de viver e contar Noronha. A ideia é criar um espaço de celebração, troca e reconhecimento da comunidade, conectando o resgate da memória da ilha às expressões artísticas, à cultura oceânica e às reflexões sobre o presente e o futuro da ilha”, afirmou a idealizadora do evento, Cynthia Mayra Nascimento Rodrigues.

A condutora de visitantes Silvia Souza e o historiador Ikaro Silvestre vão apresentar o projeto “Entre Mares e Caminhos”, que resgata histórias e aspectos da trajetória de Noronha.

O festival também terá apresentações de dança popular da ilha, promovidas pelo Grupo Cultural Dona Nanete, como o Maracatu Nação Noronha ( veja vídeo abaixo) .

O evento também terá rodas de conversas sobre turismo, sustentabilidade, comunicação, cultura e identidade. Moradores antigos da ilha vão participar de encontros para compartilhar histórias, vivências e tradições locais.

A programação inclui ainda a palestra “O mar que nos une: Cultura oceânica, liderança e o futuro de Noronha”, comandada por Henrique Pistilli Martins de Oliveira.

Além das atividades no palco, o Festei terá três oficinas. A de Arte com Fuxico, com Magna Flor, será realizada das 16h às 17h. A oficina de Papel Machê, com Lili Cavalcanti, ocorre das 17h30 às 18h30. Já a de Inovação em Mosaico, com Rosa Morais, será das 19h às 20h.

articles.title: Romero Ferro dilui Cazuza no piseiro, rejeita culpa religiosa com Catto, sofre com Luiz Lins e normaliza os desejos entre joias e bijuterias do álbum 'Ouro' | G1
articles.body:
Romero Ferro canta com Àttooxxá e Ylana em 'Ouro', álbum que lançará amanhã, quinta-feira, 27 de agosto, com repertório basicamente autoral — Foto: Gabriel Mesgo / Divulgação

♬ Quando lançou o frevo “Carnaval do desejo” em fevereiro do ano passado, às vésperas do Carnaval de 2025, Romero Ferro revelou que aprontava o álbum “Ouro”, fecho de trilogia iniciada há dez anos com o disco “Arsênico” (2016) e desenvolvida após três anos com o álbum “Ferro” (2019).

Um ano e meio depois de “Carnaval do desejo”, o cantor e compositor pernambucano enfim apresenta “Ouro” e – já na foto feita por Gabriel Mesgo para a capa do álbum que aporta amanhã, 27 de agosto, nos aplicativos de áudio – Romero sinaliza que “Ouro” está enterrado nas raízes do artista, nascido em Garanhuns (PE), no coração do agreste pernambucano.

Com essas raízes filtradas por antenas que captam os sons do mundo contemporâneo, o álbum “Ouro” reveste com beats gêneros musicais como brega, brega-funk, coco, maracatu, forró, baião e rock.

“Meio do caminho” traça a rota biográfica desse menino do mato que cresceu ouvindo o conterrâneo Dominguinhos (1941 – 2013) – evocado na faixa com sample intencionalmente distorcido de gravação de “Isso aqui tá bom demais” (1985) – e, no meio do percurso, beijou outro menino e encontrou a própria turma.

A rota sonora e existencial do álbum parte da música-título “Ouro” – gravada com o grupo Coco Raízes de Arcoverde – e inclui feats de Romero Ferro com Àttooxxá (cujo batidão encorpa “ExFinge”) e Luiz Lins, cantor e compositor pernambucano com quem o artista se une e se afina na sofrência de “Covardia”.

Ainda na seara romântica, a canção “Da eternidade ao fim” versa harmonicamente sobre um amor em paz, como tema de filme-clichê da Sessão da Tarde, como entrega a letra. Já “Safofo” põe a pimenta do desejo na fofura do amor com som típico dos bares e clubes do Nordeste do Brasil onde brega, brega-funk e piseiro convivem em harmonia.

Essa pimenta arde mais em “Amor proibido”, música de alto teor erótico, recorrente no repertório de um artista da comunidade LGBTQIA+ que sempre brincou o Carnaval do desejo sem culpa. O prazer carnal também é o mote de “Racional (Tu tu)”, tema de pegada popular.

Já trazer Cazuza (1958 – 1990) para o universo do piseiro resultou na diluição da contundência da letra escrita pelo poeta para o rock “O tempo não para” (Arnaldo Brandão e Cazuza, 1988), faixa em que o álbum “Ouro” perde alguns quilates.

Entre joias e bijuterias, equacionadas em álbum cujo repertório autoral balança, Romero Ferro divide com a conterrânea pernambucana Ylana o canto de “O preço que a alma aguenta” – música sobre a resiliência diante das perdas e danos sofridos no caminho da vida – e celebra a existência no canto efusivo de “Mistério da mistura”, convite à festa da vida vivida na rua.

No fecho da rota de “Ouro”, o álbum ganha energia roqueira em “Deus me livre desse céu”, tema em que Romero Ferro e Catto rejeitam a culpa religiosa imposta por credos e seitas nas almas de meninos do mato e da cidade que, em algum ponto do caminho, põem fé no próprio amor e desejo. É quando Romero Ferro normaliza os desejos que o álbum “Ouro” mais brilha.

Capa do álbum 'Ouro', de Romero Ferro — Foto: Gabriel Mesgo com design de RozProduz / Divulgação

articles.title: 'Sempre vou amá-la': Miley Cyrus publica mensagem para madrinha Dolly Parton  | G1
articles.standfirst: Madrinha de Miley Cyrus, cantora foi lembrada pela artista em uma homenagem que destacou a relação íntima entre as duas e o vínculo construído pela música.
articles.summary: Madrinha de Miley Cyrus, cantora foi lembrada pela artista em uma homenagem que destacou a relação íntima entre as duas e o vínculo construído pela música.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton e Miley Cyrus cantam “Jolene” durante a 61ª edição do Grammy Awards, em Los Angeles, em 10 de fevereiro de 2019 — Foto: Matt Sayles/Invision/AP/Arquivo

Miley Cyrus publicou nesta quarta-feira (26) uma homenagem à cantora Dolly Parton, que morreu na terça-feira (25), aos 80 anos. Madrinha de Miley, Dolly mantinha uma relação próxima com a artista que ia além das parcerias profissionais.

Na mensagem, Miley afirmou que a sensação de perder a "tia Dolly" era difícil demais para ser compartilhada e disse que os momentos mais especiais entre as duas permaneceriam privados.

A cantora também relembrou uma das últimas conversas que teve com Dolly, sobre "música e metamorfose", e disse acreditar que a madrinha gostaria que ela transformasse o luto em uma canção e seguisse em frente.

"Tenho um anjo ao meu lado. Sempre tive", escreveu Miley.

Ao encerrar a homenagem, Miley afirmou que sempre amará Dolly e continuará tentando deixá-la orgulhosa. Ela também lamentou a perda para familiares, amigos e fãs da cantora: "Estamos juntos nessa perda e vamos enxergá-la em todas as coisas mais bonitas".

"A sensação de perder minha tia Dolly vai além do que parece certo compartilhar. Nossos momentos mais sagrados foram privados e continuarão assim — nos bastidores, por trás do glamour e guardados entre nossos corações.

O que eu SEI é que Dolly gostaria que eu sentisse tudo isso, escrevesse uma música sobre isso e depois seguisse em frente, sendo forte. Tenho um anjo ao meu lado. Sempre tive. Uma das nossas últimas conversas foi sobre música e metamorfose.

Eu sempre vou amá-la e querer deixá-la orgulhosa. Meu coração se parte pelo mundo, pela família dela e pelos amigos que sentirão profundamente a sua falta. Estamos juntos nessa perda e vamos enxergá-la em todas as coisas mais bonitas".

Lenda da música country, a cantora e atriz Dolly Parton morreu nesta terça (25), aos 80 anos. A informação foi confirmada pela família em um vídeo nas redes sociais.

"Esse anúncio em vídeo é algo que Dolly me pediu há anos, antes que eu tivesse absorvido totalmente como uma realidade no futuro", disse Bryan Seaver, sobrinho e chefe da segurança da cantora.

Dolly enfrentava problemas de saúde desde a morte do marido, Carl Dean, que morreu em março de 2025. Ela cancelou uma residência de shows em maio deste ano. Em entrevista à revista "People", publicada no dia 21, ela disse que "não prestou atenção [aos próprios problemas]" enquanto cuidava do marido.

"Mas ainda estou trabalhando e há muitas coisas que eu ainda quero conquistar", acrescentou.

Conhecida pela voz marcante, pelas perucas loiras e por seus figurinos extravagantes, Dolly construiu um império no entretenimento a partir de suas origens humildes no estado americano do Tennessee.

Com mais de 3 mil músicas em seu catálogo, a artista se consolidou como um ícone da cultura pop e expandiu sua atuação para além da música country, transitando pelo pop, bluegrass e pela era disco.

Sua trajetória na música e no cinema se tornou parte do cânone da cultura americana. Ao longo de sua carreira, Dolly compôs sucessos atemporais que se tornaram clássicos, regravados por artistas do calibre de Beyoncé e Tina Turner. São dela músicas como "Jolene", "9 to 5" e "Coat of Many Colors".

Também foi Dolly quem escreveu e lançou a balada romântica "I Will Always Love You", posteriormente gravada por Whitney Houston para o filme "O Guarda-Costas".

articles.title: Eleições 2026 Piauí: veja a agenda dos candidatos nesta quarta (26) | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha de Elizeu Aguiar, Francisco Jurity, Geraldo Carvalho, Gustavo Henrique, Joel Rodrigues, Lúcia Santos, Lourdes Melo, Professor Gisvaldo, Rafael Fonteles, Ravenna Castro e Santiago Belizário.
articles.summary: Candidatos ao governo do Piauí realizam caminhadas e apresentam propostas para saúde e assistência social em agendas de campanha nesta quarta-feira (26).
articles.body:
Eleições 2026: Candidatos ao governo no Piauí — Foto: Montagem/g1

Candidatos ao Governo do Piauí realizaram caminhadas, panfletagens, visitas, entrevistas, gravações para o horário eleitoral, reuniões e encontros com apoiadores nesta quarta-feira (26), em Teresina.

O primeiro turno de votação será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato, em ordem alfabética:

Pela manhã, o candidato realizou gravações de vídeos para o período eleitoral. Ele não teve compromissos de campanha durante a tarde ou noite.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou caminhada e panfletagem no bairro Pirajá, na Zona Norte de Teresina, e visitou a Universidade Estadual do Piauí (Uespi). No período da tarde, concedeu entrevista para uma emissora de TV e participou de caminhada e panfletagem no bairro Matinha.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou caminhada no Conjunto Porto Alegre, na Zona Sul de Teresina. Em seguida, seguiu para a avenida comercial dos conjuntos Esplanada e Irmã Dulce e conversou com comerciantes da região. Também realizou gravações de conteúdos para as redes sociais.

No período da tarde, participou de uma reunião com a coordenação de campanha, realizou gravações para o horário eleitoral e também esteve na avenida principal do Promorar para conversar com trabalhadores e outros frequentadores.

Durante a manhã, o candidato participou de uma caminhada na Avenida Principal do Dirceu, na Zona Sudeste de Teresina. Durante a agenda, defendeu a integração entre o governo do estado e os municípios para reestruturar hospitais públicos e ampliar a oferta de serviços de saúde .

“Nós estamos no Grande Dirceu. Aqui, nós temos hospitais municipais que precisam que o Estado se junte ao município, reestruturada, mais resolutividade, trazer as especialidades médicas, os exames de imagem, e aí você traz a saúde para mais perto. Quando você fala na reestruturação dos hospitais regionais, nós estamos desafogando a saúde de Teresina. Se a gente dá resolutividade aos hospitais regionais, a gente desafoga o atendimento da saúde do Hospital de Urgência de Teresina, por exemplo, e, com essa parceria com os municípios, para dar mais resolutividade aos hospitais que estão nos bairros, como aqui na região sudeste, nós vamos ter a saúde atendendo o povo mais perto de onde eles moram”, declarou durante a caminhada.

Em seguida, realizou entrevistas e fez gravações para o período eleitoral.

“Nós estamos vendo que a feirinha está sofrendo de falta de estrutura. A gente vê a feira prejudicada, esvaziada pela violência também, pela falta de segurança. Está faltando o governo, o Estado, a presença de quem governa, para dar infraestrutura, segurança, para que as pessoas possam trabalhar, ganhar seu dinheiro e desenvolver o nosso Estado. Do plano de governo, nós vamos ver isso: infraestrutura, serviços essenciais. E, com isso funcionando, vamos poder trazer empreendimento tanto de fora quanto os nossos piauienses, para poderem empreender. A gente precisa de geração de emprego. Mas, gerando emprego, nós também precisamos de pessoas qualificadas. Então, para desenvolver, gerar emprego e renda, uma coisa está ligada à outra. Diante de tudo isso, o piauiense, com o seu trabalho, é quem vai desenvolver o estado", disse.

Ainda pela manhã, ela participou do lançamento de um podcast. No período da tarde, a candidata manteve a agenda fechada para atendimento médico.

Pela manhã, a candidata realizou um encontro com um assessor. Durante a tarde, participou de uma reunião política.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou panfletagem no Centro de Teresina. No período da tarde, concedeu entrevista para uma emissora de TV, participou do lançamento de um livro e realizou panfletagem em praças do Centro.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou caminhada no Mercado do Parque Piauí, na Zona Sul de Teresina. Na agenda, afirmou que pretende atuar como um “governador-prefeito” e destacou a necessidade de investimentos nos serviços públicos .

Não se tem segurança se não tem um bom salário para os policiais. Nós vamos fazer concurso público e dar um salário digno aos professores e aos policiais”, declarou.

Ainda pela manhã, concedeu entrevista a um programa de rádio. No período da tarde, realizou caminhada na Avenida Principal do Dirceu.

“Colocamos no nosso programa de governo o Pacto Pela Pessoa Idosa. Do mesmo jeito que tem sido um sucesso o Pacto Pela Criança do Piauí, com medidas intersetoriais e interinstitucionais, queremos fazer algo semelhante focando na pessoa idosa. Com ações que vão percorrer várias secretarias, a Secretaria de Saúde, Secretaria de Educação, Secretaria de Assistência Social, de Cultura, de Esportes, pois os nossos idosos são um conjunto de pessoas cada vez mais numeroso, e é bom que seja assim, e precisam ter qualidade de vida durante toda sua vida. Visitadores domiciliares é algo que estamos colocando no plano, semelhante ao que acontece com os agentes comunitários de saúde”, destacou o candidato à reeleição.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Chose Her Funeral Song More Than a Decade Ago & Left an Unreleased Song to Be Heard in 2046
articles.summary: "I'm sure they'll be playing 'I Will Always Love You' when I die, just like they did with Whitney Houston," she said in a 2015 interview -- but she had a dif...
articles.body:
Dolly Parton spent her life turning her own experiences, memories and emotions into music. Even after death, her songs will continue to tell her story — including two that show just how thoughtfully she considered her musical legacy.

The country music icon, who died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer, had already decided what song she wanted played at her funeral more than a decade before her death. And, in true Dolly fashion, she also left behind another song that she specifically instructed would not be heard until her 100th birthday in 2046.

In a 2014 interview with Entertainment Weekly , Parton was asked what song she would want played at her funeral. While many might have expected "I Will Always Love You" — the song she famously wrote and recorded and then later watched become an even bigger hit through Whitney Houston 's rendition — Parton had something more personal in mind.

"I'm sure they'll be playing 'I Will Always Love You' when I die, just like they did with Whitney Houston," she told the outlet at the time. But when it came to the song she actually wanted for her own funeral, she chose "If We Never Meet Again," an old country-gospel hymn with a particularly meaningful connection to her family.

The song had been her father's favorite, and it was performed at his funeral. Parton said she hoped the same song would one day be sung at hers.

The choice is fitting, given the song's message about separation and the hope of being reunited in the afterlife.

Her funeral plans were indeed something Parton had considered in advance. Her representatives confirmed Tuesday that she requested a small, private service for immediate family. Her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, also shared that Parton wanted to be laid to rest in a "beautiful bed of plush cotton."

But Parton's planning for the music that would remain until after her death went beyond her funeral. At Dollywood's DreamMore Resort in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, sits a locked chestnut box containing a recording of an unreleased Parton song called "My Place in History." The song was written in 2015 , the same year the resort opened, and Parton specifically arranged for it to be unveiled on what would have been her 100th birthday: Jan. 19, 2046.

Inside the box is a CD containing the recording, along with a CD player so that future generations will be able to hear it, outwardly a Dolly time capsule. The country legend even acknowledged the uncertainty of leaving technology from 2015 to be opened decades later.

"There's no telling what music is going to be by then," she wrote in her 2020 book, Dolly Parton, Songteller: My Life in Lyrics . "Hopefully, it will play and the whole thing ain't rotted."

Parton also joked that she hoped she would live long enough to hear the song herself when the box eventually opened. She was 69 when she wrote and recorded "My Place In History."

articles.title: That 'tone deaf' Callaway golf club ad and why it upset so many
articles.summary: Two major golf brands posted then deleted a controversial ad. Here's why people are reacting so strongly to it.
articles.body:
Callaway Golf and Good Good Golf are facing backlash after posting, then deleting, a controversial ad that depicted a man pushing a woman to the ground.

The video, which was removed by the golf brands on Aug. 21, was criticized for portraying violence against women. In response to the backlash, they issued an apology via social media.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand. We have since taken that content down, and sincerely apologize," the statement read.

But that didn't stop commenters from sharing their dislike of the ad on resurfaced clips.

"This is so much worse than I thought it was going to be...." one reacted . "Yeahhhhhh I don't think any women (without internalized misogyny) we're (sic) in the room when this was pitched, approved or produced," another wrote . "@CallawayGolf come on, as a girl dad this is infuriating," another wrote .

Others were personally impacted. "Ugh. That ad is so triggering. (Domestic violence) isn't a joke," someone wrote .

A 'visualization of a traumatic experience'

Melvin Williams , associate professor of communication and media studies at Pace University, says it's not surprising that people have reacted so strongly, given that media can mirror and amplify real-world atrocities like gender inequality and acts of violence against women.

"When media present abusive or violent experiences of any kind, fellow survivors enhance those depictions with their own stories, complex perspectives and healing resources," he told USA TODAY. "Satirical or not, the Callaway Golf and Good Good commercial was an infelicitous visualization of a traumatic experience far too many girls and women survivors of violence know all too well."

In a video posted to TikTok , Under The Desk News host Vitus "V" Spehar noted, "What's really interesting about this is how incredibly tone deaf and awful an idea it was, but also the fact that this is the first time that I could find that Good Good Golf had featured a female in any of their social media advertising at all."

"Apologies have been made, but the damage is kind of done. Especially when you consider that acts of violence from men upon women, where golf club is the weapon, is more common than not," Spehar added, citing a 2008 murder case and other high-profile instances where a golf club was used as a weapon.

"If you switch out a puppy for the woman then that ad would never have been approved," one user commented on the TikTok.

"Women golfers and wives of golfers definitely heard this. Big mistake, huge… we won't be buying Callaway or products/promotions advertised by Good Good," another wrote.

"The number of men I have seen repost it saying 'I don't see what the problem is' or 'America has gone soft' is actually terrifying," another said.

A history of violence against women in advertising

Unfortunately, this isn't the first time an ad has depicted something like this. There is a "detrimental history of violence against women being normalized and perpetuated in advertising as satirical content forms," Williams said.

When this happens, women and their bodies are commodified in dangerous way, according to Williams. They're dehumanized and a "spectatorship climate" is fostered where violence against them seems less abominable or even accepted, he explained.

"When it becomes acceptable, even in a satirical advertisement," Williams added, "the abuse of women is minimized, romanticized and presented to audiences as entertainment, humorous or shock value devices."

Contributing: Elizabeth Flores, USA TODAY

articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle reportedly land in U.K. with their children after 6 years in the U.S.
articles.summary: The couple's children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, are thought to be set to start school in Britain as Harry seeks to repair ties with the royal fami...
articles.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have returned to Britain with their two children and plan to resettle there, more than six years after moving to the U.S., according to multiple reports.

They are believed to have flown into the U.K. privately from California, according to the BBC said, though a spokesperson for the couple told the broadcaster, "This is not something we would comment on."

Flight tracking data showed a private charter jet from Van Nuys, California, arrived at Birmingham International Airport at 11:56 a.m. BST, the Associated Press reported.

Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, are set to begin school in Britain in September. AP reported on Aug. 19 that they had already been enrolled, citing a person close to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex who was not authorized to speak publicly.

King Charles III, who was diagnosed with an unspecified form of cancer in 2024, learned about the Sussexes' plans earlier this month, AP reported. The BBC said it understood that he "welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private and personal capacity."

The family is expected to settle in a privately owned home outside London rather than a royal property, according to AP. The Sussexes also intend to keep their home in Montecito, California, and a vacation property in Portugal. Harry and Meghan do not plan to return to being working members of the royal family.

The Daily Telegraph was the first outlet to report the plans. People magazine later reported on the move, while Reuters said a source close to Harry and Meghan had confirmed the plans.

Neither the couple's spokesperson nor Buckingham Palace has publicly confirmed the move. Harry said he had "nothing to say" when asked about the reports Wednesday night during an event with U.S. veterans in Washington.

The reported move comes as Harry has sought to repair his relationship with his family, particularly his father, Charles.

After losing a legal challenge over his security arrangements in Britain last year, Harry told the BBC that he no longer wanted the family dispute to continue. "I would love reconciliation with my family," he said at the time.

The family was in Britain as recently as last month. During that trip, Harry, Meghan and their children spent time with Charles at his Highgrove estate. The visit also reunited Charles with Archie and Lilibet for the first time since Queen Elizabeth II's platinum jubilee celebrations in 2022.

Relations between Harry and his older brother, Prince William, remain strained. Reuters reported that the brothers are still barely speaking.

Peter Hunt, a former BBC royal correspondent, said the surprise return is likely to infuriate William.

He told the Press Association, the U.K. news agency, "In the short term, Harry will be able to deepen his rapprochement with his father. And his presence back home will make it harder for his brother to duck a reconciliation. The surprise return of Harry and Meghan is likely to have left William apoplectic."

A source close to the Sussexes told AP that Harry will be able to devote more time to his charitable work in Britain, while Meghan will continue running her lifestyle business, As Ever, from the U.K.

Meghan may also return to acting, with Australian news outlet News.com.au reporting that one reason for the couple's decision to relocate to Britain was that Meghan had been offered a role in an upcoming project. A source close to the duchess did not deny the report.

Deadline reported that Meghan has had preliminary conversations about a potential role in the Netflix series The Gentlemen , which would mark her first significant acting role since her marriage to Harry in 2018.

The couple has been based in Montecito since moving to California after stepping away from royal duties in 2020.

The Telegraph reported that Harry wanted a "refuge" in the U.K. and the "freedom to enjoy British summers, see friends and come and go without the 'circus' that has surrounded recent visits."

During their years in the U.S., Harry and Meghan signed deals with Netflix and Spotify and spoke publicly about their experiences within the royal family. Harry published his memoir, Spare , which became a bestseller. Their Spotify partnership later ended, while Reuters reported that Meghan's Netflix lifestyle show was not renewed for a third season.

Harry has also spent years pursuing legal cases in Britain, including disputes involving the British press and a challenge over the level of police protection available to him and his family when they visit the country.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham declined to comment on Harry and Meghan's security arrangements in Britain, saying the funding for them was a "private matter."

articles.title: Rupert Grint To Join Broadway’s ‘Harry Potter And the Cursed Child’ In Ron Weasley Reprise
articles.summary: Rupert Grint, who played Ron Weasley in all eight of the Harry Potter films, will reprise the role on Broadway this winter, following in the footsteps of the...
articles.body:
Rupert Grint, who played Ron Weasley in all eight of the Harry Potter films, will reprise the role on Broadway this winter, following in the footsteps of the movies' Draco Malfoy and current Harry Potter and the Cursed Child star Tom Felton.

Like Felton, Grint will portray the grown-up version of the role he originated as a child in the films. But the two will not share the same Broadway stage: Grint takes on the role of Ron Weasley for 17 weeks beginning Tuesday, February 2, 2027, and continuing through Sunday, May 30, 2027. Felton, currently in the show, is expected to exit on Sunday, January 3, 2027.

Felton's casting in the show at the Lyric Theatre last November had an immediate box office impact, sending ticket sales and attendance soaring.

In a statement, Grint said, "Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old and I can't wait to meet him again in this stage of life. There is something so full-circle and so special about stepping back into Ron's shoes now when we are both fathers; it is somehow both very familiar and completely new. And the joy of being back on Broadway, this time in a role that defined so much of my life is truly exciting.

"The first time I saw Cursed Child onstage," he continued, "I was blown away and I can't wait to set foot back on Platform 9 ¾ and pick up where I left off. I am overjoyed to join this exceptional cast and crew at the Lyric Theatre this winter."

In a joint statement, producers Sonia Friedman and Colin Callender said, "Rupert Grint's performance as Ron Weasley in the eight Harry Potter films defined for generations what it meant to be a loyal and brave friend even in the face of adversity and hardship. We, along with all the wizarding world fans around the globe, watched Rupert grow up through his portrayal of Ron while preserving the qualities at the very heart of the character – his humor, his bravery, and of course, that unmistakably cheeky grin – like an invisible thread woven throughout the years.

"In joining our extraordinary company onstage at the Lyric Theatre in New York City," they continued, "Rupert is not simply revisiting a role from his past. He is continuing a journey he began as a child and carrying it forward with all the life and experience he has gained since filming concluded, including a career that has taken him from film to television to acclaimed stage work on both Broadway and the West End. His return creates a powerful bridge between the story audiences first fell in love with and the story of family, legacy and the passage of time that Harry Potter and the Cursed Child carries forward. We feel enormously privileged not only to welcome a world-class actor to our Broadway company, but to welcome back the actor who made Ron Weasley so beloved."

Grint made his Broadway debut in the 2014 production of Terrence McNally's It's Only a Play opposite Matthew Broderick and Nathan Lane. In the UK, he made his West End debut in the production of Jez Butterworth's acclaimed play Mojo , starring as the lead opposite Ben Whishaw.

Grint most recently starred in Hanna Bergholm's film Nightborn which premiered at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival, and was released by IFC. He'll next star in Paramount Pictures' film Ebenezer , opening in theaters on November 13.

His other credits include M. Night Shyamalan's Servant , which ran for four seasons on Apple TV, and the director's feature film Knock at the Cabin . He's also appeared in Guillermo del Toro's anthology series Cabinet of Curiosities on Netflix, among other roles.

Nathan Gallagher is speaking out after his arrest on domestic violence charges in Australia. The Below Deck Mediterranean star says the public has not heard the full story surrounding the December 2025 incident. Gallagher also claims he has video footage, messages, and other records that could provide more context.

Nathan Gallagher says he has evidence that offers another side of his arrest

In a statement to Rolling Stone , Gallagher said public reporting represents "only one side" of what he described as a complicated situation. "But I will not accept being portrayed solely through one person's account of a relationship when there is another side and evidence relating to it," Gallagher added.

He said he has video from the night in question, along with messages and other records. Gallagher also offered to provide relevant footage for review.

However, Rolling Stone said it requested those materials before publication and did not receive them.

The Nathan Gallagher arrest stems from an alleged Dec. 26, 2025, incident at a Sydney-area apartment complex. New South Wales Police charged him with assault occasioning actual bodily harm, intentionally choking a person without consent and common assault.

Police arrested Gallagher the following day. He later received conditional bail and is due back in Burwood Local Court on Sept. 1. The Nathan Gallagher charges and arrest were previously detailed here.

A separate court matter also involves Gael Cameron, Gallagher's former partner and Below Deck co-star. Court records show an Apprehended Violence Application involving Gallagher and Cameron.

Gallagher said he has made mistakes and would take responsibility for his own actions. Still, he rejected being defined solely by one account of the relationship. The Below Deck arrest has drawn attention while Season 11 continues airing. Gallagher also said his priority is his son and finding a way to co-parent peacefully.

Cameron has not publicly responded to Gallagher's new statement. For now, Gallagher's case continues in Australia. He will return to Burwood Local Court on Sept. 1

articles.summary: También participó en ‘Solo en casa 2’, con Macaulay Culkin
articles.body: Tim Curry, conocido actor de terror, ha muerto a los 80 años, después de sufrir un derrame cerebral en 2012 que le dejó postrado en una silla de ruedas, aunque eso no le impidió seguir trabajando. Así lo ha informado el portal estadounidense TMZ, sin desvelarse aún la causa de la muerte. Su salto a la fama se debió gracias a su papel como científico travestido Dr. Frank-N-Furter, en ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’, u otros papeles como Pennywise el payaso, en ‘It’, en la primera adaptación cinematográfica de la novela de Stephen King en 1990. Murió este martes, 25 de agosto, por la noche, en su casa de Los Ángeles, Estados Unidos. En cuanto a sus inicios, nació el 19 de abril de 1946 en Cheshire, Inglaterra, siendo su padre un capellán metodista de la Marina Real, que falleció cuando Tim tenía sólo 12 años. Curry comenzó su carrera en el mundo del cine en 1968, en una producción de ‘Hair’, en el West End, graduándose a la vez en la Universidad de Birmingham, en el Reino Unido. En esta etapa conoció al actor Richard O'Brien, guionista de ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’, para acabar trabajando en ella en la adaptación cinematográfica de Fox de 1975. En 1990 logró uno de sus papeles más recordados: Pennywise, en una adaptación de dos partes de ‘It’, emitida por ABC. Eso sí, también hizo comedia, mostrando su versatilidad, participando en ‘Solo en casa 2’ (1992), interpretando al recepcionista del hotel donde se alojaba Kevin (Macaulay Culkin). A mediados de 2012, la salud de Tim Curry sufrió un severo revés tras padecer un accidente cerebrovascular que afectó drásticamente su movilidad, llevándolo a depender de una silla de ruedas. La noticia no se conoció hasta un año después, cuando se mostró de forma pública, eso sí, a pesar de las secuelas físicas, el intérprete no interrumpió su carrera comenzando a realizar locución y doblaje de personajes, como ‘Star Wars: The Clone Wars’, dando voz a personajes icónicos como el Canciller Palpatine y Darth Sidious. En su momento, durante una charla en el Academy Museum de Los Ángeles, explicó: “Todavía no puedo caminar, por eso estoy en esta ridícula silla, y eso me limita mucho. Así que no podré cantar ni bailar muy pronto. Tengo serios problemas con mi pierna izquierda”. “Yo siempre tuve mucha suerte, hasta ese viernes 13 de julio, cuando tuve el derrame. Estaba recibiendo un masaje y el masajista me dijo: ‘Estoy preocupado por ti, quiero llamar a una ambulancia’. Y lo hizo”, destacó. “Un sanitario muy simpático me dijo que me iba a poner morfina, así que yo le dije: ‘Adelante”, sentenció sobre lo ocurrido.

articles.title: Blake Lively Awarded $400,000 in Attorneys’ Fees in Justin Baldoni Case
articles.summary: A judge on Wednesday awarded Blake Lively about $400,000 in attorneys’ fees in her dispute with “It Ends With Us” co-star Justin Baldoni, well short of the $...
articles.body:
A judge on Wednesday awarded Blake Lively about $400,000 in attorneys' fees in her dispute with "It Ends With Us" co-star Justin Baldoni, well short of the $8 million she had sought .

Lively and Baldoni settled their 18-month legal war in May, avoiding a federal trial that was scheduled for later that month. At the time, the only loose end was Lively's motion for attorneys' fees for having to defend against Baldoni's failed defamation suit.

Judge Lewis Liman on Wednesday awarded her $363,000 in attorneys' fees and another $44,000 in court costs. In his ruling , the judge found that Lively was entitled only to the "reasonable" fees related to defending against the defamation suit.

Liman ruled that while the attorneys' billing rates were "not unreasonable," given the high stakes of the case and the complexity of the issues, "(t)he number of hours for which Lively seeks reimbursement is unreasonable."

Lively had asked for $7.5 million in attorneys' fees and another $540,000 in court costs. Instead, the judge awarded her just double what the New York Times was awarded for defending itself from Baldoni's defamation case.

Lively filed a complaint with the California Civil Rights Department in December 2024, alleging that Baldoni and Wayfarer Studios had launched an online smear campaign against her in retaliation for raising complaints about sexual harassment on the set of "It Ends With Us."

Baldoni fired back with a defamation suit, accusing Lively and her husband, Ryan Reynolds, of concocting fake allegations as part of an effort to hijack creative control of the film. He also sued the Times for running a story drawn largely on on the civil rights complaint. That suit was dismissed on the grounds that Lively's claims were protected by litigation privilege and the paper's coverage was a fair report of the proceedings.

Lively sought compensation under a 2023 California law meant to discourage frivolous defamation suits against accusers who come forward with allegations of sexual assault. Lively initially asked for treble damages and punitive damages as well, but Liman previously ruled that those were not available under federal law.

articles.title: Tim Curry, of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' and 'It' fame, dies at 80
articles.summary: The legendary British actor reportedly died Tuesday night at his Los Angeles home at age 80.
articles.body:
Legendary actor and The Rocky Horror Picture Show star Tim Curry died on Tuesday night in Los Angeles at the age of 80. TMZ was first to report the news. Curry's longtime friend and manager, Marcia Hurwitz, confirmed his death to the Associated Press . The cause of his death has not been disclosed.

The British actor suffered a stroke in 2012 that left him partially paralyzed, and he had been dealing with serious health issues for more than a decade. According to TMZ, police responded to his home at 11:23 p.m. on Tuesday. There is no foul play suspected.

Curry is best known for his wide range of comedic and often villainous roles, accompanied by his unmistakable, rich, theatrical laugh. He started his professional acting career in the late 1960s, shortly after graduating from the University of Birmingham in the U.K.

The actor told CBS's Sunday Morning last year that acting excited him, because it was "The freedom of being somebody else."

Curry's first paid acting gig was a 1968 London production of Hair, where he met actor Richard O'Brien, who wrote the 1975 musical comedy The Rocky Horror Picture Show . It was then that Curry landed his breakout role as the corset-and-fishnet-stocking-wearing Dr. Frank-N-Furter, which later became a cult classic.

"He gave a lot of teenagers permission to be different, and I'm very happy that he did have that power," Curry told CBS, referring to the flamboyant character.

In 1990, Curry also portrayed the terrifying character Pennywise the clown in Stephen King's adaptation of "It." His other widely known roles included Mr. Hector, the Plaza Hotel's nosy personal concierge in 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York .

Curry's other memorable movie credits include Annie (1982), Clue (1985), The Hunt for Red October (1990), The Three Musketeers (1993), Muppet Treasure Island (1996) , Addams Family Reunion (1998) and Scary Movie 2 (2001).

While Curry played a wide range of roles, he wrote in his 2025 memoir "Vagabond" that he was not like any of them. "The distinctions between who I really am and who I've pretended to be as an actor have proven to be a source of great disappointment to some audiences," he wrote. "It has not caused me much personal distress beyond the periodic necessity to deter stalkers."

Over the course of his career, Curry also earned three Tony nominations for his performances in "Spamalot," "My Favorite Year" and "Amadeus." He earned a 1994 Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Drama Series for his multi-role performance on Tales from the Crypt .

"I don't fear death, I try to avoid it," Curry told CBS with a chuckle, "as I think we all do."

"But I suspect that in the end I will welcome it … I think it may be comforting to go bye- bye, and I want to earn it," Curry said with a laugh.

articles.title: Daniel Sancho podría tardar 20 años en volver a España desde Tailandia
articles.standfirst: El país estudia un cambio en su sistema legal
articles.summary: El país estudia un cambio en su sistema legal
articles.body: Daniel Sancho está esperando, en la cárcel de Surat Thani, a la lectura pública de la sentencia por el asesinato del cirujano colombiano Edwin Arrieta, en agosto de 2023. El recurso presentado por la defensa del español busca que la sentencia pase de asesinato con premeditación a homicidio imprudente. De esta forma, su regreso a España para cumplir condena podría ser más rápido. Pero esta aspiración se ha visto truncada, según ha informado periodista Joaquín Campos en Telecinco, por una nueva propuesta legal. La legislación de Tailandia, siempre en base a las explicaciones de Campos, se plantea endurecer su burocracia y obligar a que los condenados a cadena perpetua no puedan abandonar el país en un mínimo de 20 años. Si esta medida obtiene finalmente luz verde, el regreso de Daniel Sancho a España se demoraría mucho más de lo previsto. Todos los planteamientos de la defensa del español quedarían devastados si esta medida se aplica. El periodista Joaquín Campos ha asegurado en Telecinco que este posible cambio en la legalidad tailandesa está avanzado. "El departamento de instituciones penitenciarias estudiaba una nueva normativa y ya tiene el borrador que se va a hacer oficial", ha indicado. Eso sí, no es seguro que finalmente vez la luz ni tampoco que, en caso de hacerlo, afecte de forma retroactiva a Daniel Sancho. En España, por ejemplo, existe el principio de irretroactividad de las leyes penales, mediante el que el acusado no puede ser castigado por un delito con una severidad mayor a la que existía en las normativas en el momento en el que sucedió. La Constitución de Tailandia también plantea, en su artículo 29, este mismo principio. Por otra parte, el periodista Javier Campos ha señalado que este cambio en el sistema legal de Tailandia surgió a raíz de la excarcelación de un famoso narcotraficante.

articles.title: Blake Lively awarded $400,000 in legal fees over dismissed Justin Baldoni lawsuit
articles.summary: Blake Lively can recover about $400,000 in attorneys’ fees from Justin Baldoni’s production company over his defamation lawsuit against her, a federal judge ruled Wednesday.
articles.body: Blake Lively can recover about $400,000 in attorneys’ fees from Justin Baldoni’s production company over his defamation lawsuit against her, a federal judge ruled Wednesday. Lively had been seeking $8 million. U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman dismissed Baldoni’s defamation and extortion lawsuit against Lively last year, and she was allowed to move forward with a request for financial damages under a California #MeToo-era law. Liman wrote in his ruling that while “counsel’s rates were not unreasonable… the number of hours for which Lively seeks reimbursement is unreasonable.” He also rejected her request for fees related to media relations expenses and some travel. In a statement, Lively’s attorneys, Esra Hudson and Michael Gottlieb, said, in part, “Blake Lively’s case was never about money — it was about accountability. She lifted the curtain for other victims, and set the precedent for others to come forward and expose similar conduct. This result demonstrates that the legal system is not as easily manipulated as social media, and still functions as a force for accountability.” Lively was seeking $8,035,040.88 in fees and costs, comprised of $7,495,526.87 in attorneys’ fees and costs in the amount of $539,514.01. Liman awarded her $363,245.40 in attorneys’ fees and $44,206.35 in costs. Baldoni attorney Bryan Freedman framed the judge’s ruling of the much smaller award as a victory for his client. “Judge Liman clearly considered the ‘outrageous and unreasonable’ $8 million plus demand and, in rejecting it, awarded only 5 percent of the amount sought in legal fees and costs,” Freedman said in a statement on Wednesday. “The ruling is a significant victory for my clients and sends a clear message that, no matter how powerful you may be, the courtroom is not a place to take advantage of the law for your own personal gain.” Lively and Baldoni settled their yearslong legal dispute in early May. Terms of the settlement were not disclosed. A source familiar with the matter previously confirmed to NBC News that no money changed hands. The settlement headed off what had promised to be a blockbuster trial in New York. Lively accused Baldoni of sexual harassment during the production of the 2024 movie “It Ends With Us,” which he directed. Lively had also alleged that Baldoni’s company, Wayfarer Studios, retaliated against her after she complained about allegations of misconduct on the set of the film. Baldoni vehemently denied Lively’s claims. In January 2025, Baldoni countersued Lively and her husband, “Deadpool” actor Ryan Reynolds, alleging defamation and extortion. He argued that Lively and Reynolds tried to wreck his reputation and accused her of using her grievances as a way to “seize control” of the movie. Baldoni also brought a defamation suit against The New York Times over an article headlined: “‘We Can Bury Anyone’: Inside a Hollywood Smear Machine.” Liman tossed out both suits last year.

articles.title: Two separate mini-Bigfoot sightings reported in an area of Pennsylvania with a history of activity
articles.summary: Two mini-Bigfoot creatures standing just three and a half feet tall were reportedly spotted on a farm in Southwest Pennsylvania, Stan Gordon reports.
articles.body: Reports out of Southwest Pennsylvania indicate that people are seeing some odd creatures wandering around outside. They've been described as Bigfoot encounters, but these aren't your typical 8-foot giants. These are sightings of what Penn Live reports are "mini-Bigfoots." The two separate incidents took place last Tuesday, Aug. 18, and Wednesday, Aug. 19, and involve Bigfoot-like creatures that are no taller than five feet. The first encounter, which was reported to researcher Stan Gordon, took place on a farm in Indiana County, Pennsylvania. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS The witness, Gordon reported, was wrapping up a chore at one of the farm buildings on the property when she heard what sounded like something being thrown around. As she exited the building she "noticed a figure crouching behind trees approximately 60 feet away. She then saw a second, similar figure crouched near the first." She claims the two figures jumped up and started running around as if they were playing. She watched them for several minutes, describing them as walking upright on two legs and standing about three and a half feet tall. "Their bodies were covered with straggly, medium-length, light brown hair," Gordon noted from the witness' account. DAD AND HIS KIDS THINK THEY'VE CAPTURED BIGFOOT ON VIDEO AFTER SPOTTING SOMETHING IN THE WOODS "Neither appeared to have a visible neck. Their heads seemed to rest directly on their shoulders. Their faces were darker brown than the rest of their bodies, and their eyes appeared round and dark brown." The witness, unfortunately, didn’t have her phone with her. But she went on to describe them as having slender arms reminding her of a young child's arms and making noises that sounded like a baby cooing. The encounter came to an end when she sneezed and the two mini-Bigfoot spotted her. She ran home and told her husband about it. The family dog was afraid to go outside after the incident, and she was awakened one night by a sound similar to the cooing she says she heard. Her husband heard loud knocks the day of the sighting, but didn’t witness anything himself. The second of the encounters took place the following night around 8:00 p.m. in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania. A driver along a rural road says she spotted a creature covered in hair running up a hill. TWO LADIES, A DOG, A LIGHTHOUSE AND A POSSIBLE BIGFOOT ENCOUNTER ON A BEACH IN MICHIGAN The witness only saw the creature for a few seconds, but says she got a good look at it. She estimated the height to be just five feet tall. She says it moved on two legs and was covered with charcoal-gray hair. "Its head was somewhat dome-shaped, with no apparent neck. The arms were long and swung as it moved. Its nose appeared slightly flat with flared nostrils," Gordon noted. "The witness did not notice any ears. Its eyes were small and dark. She saw only one hair-covered leg clearly as the creature spun around and retreated down the hillside." This general area of Pennsylvania has had Bigfoot and UFO sightings before, according to Gordon. But there's nothing to connect these recent sightings with any of those prior reports. As is the case with a lot of sightings, this one did not come with any supporting physical evidence. Not even a blurry picture of what is probably a shadow. articles.title: Let's look back on the best moments (read: crashes) from the World Humanoid Robot Games
articles.summary: Videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games show android athletes crashing, boxing, and high-jumping in hilarious fashion as algorithms spread the clips.
articles.body: Social media algorithms can be a treacherous thing, but sometimes they just bring pure, unleaded delight, as has been the case with videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games. My usual Instagram feed full of guitars, motorsports news, and clips from Amish softball games (which are phenomenal, by the way) was suddenly hijacked by video after video of humanoid robots hitting the track, boxing, and high-jumping at their human masters' bidding. It's a beautiful thing... until they snap and enslave us all, but damn, until then it's hilarious. CHINESE ROBOT BREAKS HUMAN WORLD RECORD IN BEIJING HALF-MARATHON So, with the Games drawing to a close, I wanted to take a walk down memory lane at some of the Games' best moments. Sure, there was the bot that beat Usain Bolt's 100-meter record, but I prefer the more light-hearted lowlights. I'm talking about any video in which the 100-meter-running bots crash into a pad because, despite the incredible tech on display, no one has figured out how to give these android athletes any kind of braking procedure. HUMANOID ROBOTS JUST GOT A WORKPLACE SAFETY SYSTEM Now, I don't mean to sit here and play armchair robotics expert, but how is it that not one poindexter in the robot-building bunch has worked out a sensor that tells the robot it's about to plow into a crash pad? Think of cars with adaptive cruise control or even fully driverless cars. Yet, with that tech available, the best we can do for those robots is treat them like crash test dummies? HUMANOID ROBOT SKIN SENSES PEOPLE BEFORE CONTACT I'd want to enslave humanity too, if that was how I was treated. But, hey, I still love the crashes. When they happen, the sensors that are on board go completely haywire and send the bots into some kind of Raygun Olympic breakdancing routine. No one had a worse time, however, than this poor bot who competed in weightlifting and gave us the biggest choke job of all time. Poor guy... probably got swirlied in the locker room too. What an event and what a content factory the World Humanoid Robot Games proved to be. articles.title: Italian Festival returns to Endicott for 19th year running
articles.summary: ENDICOTT, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – Get ready to savor the sounds and flavors of Little Italy this Friday. GUSTO! Italian Festival is returning to the Northside of...
articles.body:
ENDICOTT, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) - Get ready to savor the sounds and flavors of Little Italy this Friday.

GUSTO! Italian Festival is returning to the Northside of Endicott for its 19th year.

The festival continues to grow in terms of its attendance, footprint and number of vendors, over 40 this year.

The primary focus is on Italian food, with meatballs, pizza, sausage and peppers, lamb spiedies and a wide variety of Italian desserts and pastries. Although there will be Greek and soul food vendors as well.

There will also be a wide variety of live music on multiple stages.

Little Italy Endicott Board Member Loreta Paniccia says GUSTO! helps bring awareness to the group's efforts to revitalize the neighborhood.

"GUSTO! is a capstone activity that we hold. A community event that brings in support to our vendors and our businesses, but it's more attention to our bigger mission which is supporting our neighborhood and continuing to build community and enhancing this area as much as we can," Paniccia says.

There will also be plenty of fun activities for kids including face painting, arts and crafts, yard games and magic shows.

The evening will conclude with a fireworks show over George W. Johnson Park.

GUSTO! runs from 4:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. Friday and is free to attend.

articles.title: Rockstar finally releases statement regarding ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ leaks, leaving fans even more confused
articles.summary: Rockstar Games broke its silence on the "Grand Theft Auto VI" leaks, but key phrases in the statement sparked an uproar among frustrated fans.
articles.body: Last week, a series of gameplay leaks of the much anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" captivated the video game community. A social media account by the name of CyberLeek posted a number of videos playing what appeared to be a full build of the game, including one in which they flew an airplane through downtown Vice City, a fictionalized version of Miami. Game developer Rockstar remained silent for nearly a week after the leaks, despite CyberLeek’s continued calls for them to respond. GAMING-WORLD VETERAN WHO RIPPED ‘WOKE’ CULTURE SCORES TRUMP-BACKED BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY WIN Wednesday morning, however, Rockstar Games broke its silence, releasing a statement and giving an update on the game’s status in the wake of the leaks. In case you couldn’t figure it out just by skimming through it, the statement didn’t go over well with many of the gaming community, as several key phrases caught fans’ attention in a negative way. For starters, Rockstar calling the leaks "heartbreaking" had plenty of fans all over the internet rolling their eyes. The big one that had everyone in an uproar, though, was toward the end of the first paragraph, where Rockstar revealed the game still isn’t finished. A game that has taken 13 years to complete still isn’t quite ready yet, and that caused fans to explode. Another line that caused some confusion was at the end of the second paragraph, where Rockstar says, "we hope everyone will wait a little bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19." Some fans incorrectly assumed that meant another delay was in the works, but I don’t believe that to be the case. With Rockstar's track record, I could see how that would be the thought process from fans. THE FIVE BEST YEARS IN VIDEO GAME HISTORY RANKED: WHICH GAMING YEAR WAS THE GREATEST EVER? Others thought the leaks and subsequent negative public response caused the developers to panic and go back to fixing the game, but this far into things I doubt that's what this is all about. Regardless of what Rockstar thought it would achieve by releasing this statement, it did little to quell the bloodlust from fans who have felt scorned by the once-beloved developer. Gamers have felt burned by the seemingly exorbitant wait for the next big Grand Theft Auto game as well as the announcement earlier this year that the game would be released solely as a digital game with no physical disc to accompany it. This was the genesis for CyberLeek’s avalanche of gameplay leaks over the past week, claiming to do so on behalf of gamers everywhere who felt as though Rockstar disregarded their core demographic with these choices and delays. One thing is for sure, we haven’t seen the last of this saga. articles.title: Why Dolly Parton could bring together Americans who agree on almost nothing
articles.summary: Dolly Parton embodied the African concept of Ubuntu — "I am because we are" — enlarging humanity through her Imagination Library and delight in others.
articles.body: Throughout her life, Dolly Parton kept reminding me of something beautiful about being human. Perhaps you noticed it too. Her death has brought an outpouring of affection from people who otherwise might agree on very little. And it leaves me wondering: What was it about Dolly? Talent alone doesn't explain it. Success doesn't explain it. Even her extraordinary generosity doesn't fully explain it. DOLLY PARTON DIES AT THE AGE OF 80: A LOOK AT HER LIFE THROUGH PHOTOS I suspect we recognized something deeper — a way of being human that somehow enlarged the humanity around her. Many years ago, my friend Archbishop Desmond Tutu introduced me to an African word that has stayed with me ever since: Ubuntu. It is often translated as "I am because we are." Over time, I have experienced Ubuntu less as a definition and more as a way of moving through the world. It is the quiet conviction that another person's life can become larger because you showed up. It is the belief that another person's humanity matters too much to be reduced to a label, a failure, a fear or someone else's judgment. Dolly Parton struck me as someone who intuitively Ubuntued her way through life. DOLLY PARTON'S ‘ALL-AMERICAN HEART’: HOW COUNTRY ICON FORGED SPECIAL BOND WITH US MILITARY In an America increasingly divided into competing camps and tribes, she was one of our great exceptions. Conservatives admired her. Liberals admired her. Christians admired her. People with no religious affiliation admired her. Rural America admired her. Urban America admired her. Dolly Parton is gone. But what we loved in her isn't. She seemed to delight in people. She didn't require that people become more like her before she could enjoy them. Want to have some of what Dolly had? Lean into Ubuntu. Most of us know what it feels like to be reduced to a label, a mistake, a fear or someone else's judgment. And most of us have encountered someone who refused to leave us there. Perhaps you've known someone who saw more in you than the labels that had been placed upon you. Perhaps you've encountered someone who made it feel safe to speak in your own voice. DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY Perhaps you've known what it feels like when another person's belief in you arrived before your belief in yourself. Perhaps you've known someone who called forth a larger version of yourself than you could yet imagine. People like this leave us feeling more alive. Perhaps that's because we are not completed in isolation. We are enlarged through encounter. I have yet to meet anyone who isn't carrying more than they should. Maybe that's why another person's humanity can feel so nourishing. Someone sees us. Believes in us. Delights in us. And something in us comes alive. I have no idea whether Dolly Parton ever heard the word Ubuntu. But I suspect she understood it instinctively. Her Imagination Library put hundreds of millions of books into the hands of children, most of whom she would never meet. The number is extraordinary. But perhaps more revealing is what it says about her: She believed in the possibilities of children she did not know. We saw that same instinct in the way she encountered people — in her easy laughter, her delight in others and her apparent belief that the person in front of her mattered. She used her success to enlarge possibilities for people far beyond herself. Dolly Ubuntued. One of the things I love most about Ubuntu is that nobody has to qualify for it. There is no means test, no dress code, no success code, no educational requirement, no preferred political party, no preferred religion, no preferred heritage, no preferred ZIP code, no VIP entrance and no secret handshake. Bring your humanity. That's it. We are changed, nourished, challenged and enlarged through our encounters with one another — sometimes most unexpectedly by people whose lives seem different from our own. In a world that constantly encourages us to sort, rank, label and separate ourselves from one another, Ubuntu offers an astonishing possibility: None of us becomes fully human alone. Your humanity strengthens mine while mine expands yours. We need one another's humanity in order to thrive. Ubuntu may help us survive difficult seasons. But its deeper promise is that we flourish. Not despite one another. Through one another. The older I get, the more convinced I become that this is not simply a beautiful idea. It is a practical truth. We are changed, nourished, challenged and enlarged through our encounters with one another — sometimes most unexpectedly by people whose lives seem different from our own. And we don't encounter this only in people whose names the world knows. It appears in teachers and neighbors, nurses and firefighters, grandparents and lifelong friends and complete strangers. In someone who saw more in you than you could see in yourself. In someone whose humanity surprised you because their life seemed so different from your own. And chances are, you've been that person for someone else. Ubuntu is not merely a word. It's a human thing — a way of helping one another flourish, of becoming more fully ourselves and of discovering that neither of us necessarily leaves an encounter unchanged. Humanity is one of the few things in life that grows when it is shared. When we strengthen another person's humanity, we strengthen our own. Dolly Parton is gone. But what we loved in her isn't. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION It is still possible every time someone refuses to reduce another person to a label. Every time someone believes in another person before that person can believe in themselves. Every time one human being calls forth something larger in another — and discovers that they, too, have been enlarged. Maybe that's some of what Dolly was showing us all along. So let's celebrate humanity. Let's celebrate the people who enlarge it. You've been Ubuntued. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Perhaps you've Ubuntued others. Let's Ubuntu together.

articles.title: Busy Philipps diagnosed with rare brain tumor after undergoing body scan her doctor told her she didn't 'need'
articles.summary: Busy Phillips revealed her grade 2 oligodendroglioma diagnosis came after a Prenuvo scan her primary care doctor initially said she didn't need.
articles.body: Busy Philipps is sharing how she was diagnosed with a rare brain tumor. During a recent interview with People magazine, the 47-year-old "Cougar Town" actress shared the terrifying moment her doctor told her she had a brain tumor, the day after her "Dawson's Creek" co-star, James Van Der Beek, died after a battle with colorectal cancer. "Dr. Devinsky says to me, 'I'm just going to say this to you the way I would want someone to say it to me,'" she recalled. 'BACHELORETTE' STAR REVEALS BRAIN TUMOR DIAGNOSIS AFTER ROUTINE HEALTH SCAN "And that was when the wind like sort of knocked out of me, and I had to sit down. He was like, 'I need you to breathe. I can hear that you're not breathing.' And I was like, 'Just tell me what's happening.' And he's like, 'This isn't any of those other things that they said it could be. This is a real tumor, and it's inside your brain, and Busy, it's got to come out. We got to take it out.'" She was then connected with Dr. John Golfinos of NYU Langone and scheduled the five-hour surgery for March 2, during which surgeons removed a 2.6-centimeter mass from her brain. The mass was then biopsied and revealed to be a grade 2 oligodendroglioma, a rare tumor that Dr. Alexandra Miller, Philipps’s neuro-oncologist at NYU Langone told People, affects 1,100 to 1,300 people a year in the U.S. She added that "it is considered malignant, but it has the best prognosis of all of the malignant gliomas." "It’s sort of defined as a cancerous tumor based on the ability of the tumor to regrow over time, rather than it looking very malignant under the microscope," Miller said. The diagnosis came after Philipps told her cousin’s husband, a doctor in Los Angeles, that she was interested in getting a Prenuvo scan but that her primary care doctor had told her in 2025, "You're super healthy. We've done all this other blood work. We've done, like, all kinds of tests. You're super healthy. There's no need for you to get one." "'Oh, I love them,'" he told Philipps about the scan. "And I was like, 'OK, cause my doctor just a few months ago said that I shouldn't get one.' He's like, 'Oh, like respectfully, don't know your doctor, but disagree. I think knowledge is power.' "And what he said really resonated with me. And I was like, 'That was kind of what I was feeling, too. I think I want to get one.' He's like, 'Well, I'd be happy to help you set that up.'" Dr. Devinsky later told her the MRI showed a tumor that needed to be removed. Philipps’ neurosurgeon, Dr. John Golfinos, told People that the early detection of the tumor ultimately made the surgery much easier, adding that had the tumor been found later, it "would have been two or three times the size."
